name: Catalan (Central)
variety: Central Catalan (Eastern dialect group), educated speech of the Barcelona area, the basis of the standard of Catalonia
sources: Carbonell, Joan F. and Llisterri, Joaquim (1992). Catalan. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 22(1-2), 53-56. Reprinted in the Handbook of the International Phonetic Association (1999), Cambridge University Press.
Wheeler, Max W. (2005). The Phonology of Catalan. Oxford University Press.
Hualde, José Ignacio (1992). Catalan. London: Routledge (Descriptive Grammars).
Recasens, Daniel (1996). Fonètica descriptiva del català. 2nd edition. Barcelona: Institut d'Estudis Catalans.
Recasens, Daniel and Espinosa, Aina (2006). Dispersion and variability of Catalan vowels. Speech Communication 48, 645-666.
Veny, Joan (1982). Els parlars catalans: síntesi de dialectologia. Palma: Moll.
Institut d'Estudis Catalans (2016). Gramàtica de la llengua catalana. Barcelona: IEC.
Prieto, Pilar (2014). The intonational phonology of Catalan. In Jun (ed.), Prosodic Typology II. Oxford University Press.
Prieto, Pilar et al. (2015). Intonational phonology of Catalan and its dialectal varieties. In Frota and Prieto (eds.), Intonation in Romance. Oxford University Press.
Ramus, Franck; Nespor, Marina; Mehler, Jacques (1999). Correlates of linguistic rhythm in the speech signal. Cognition 73, 265-292.
Grabe, Esther and Low, Ee Ling (2002). Durational variability in speech and the rhythm class hypothesis. In Gussenhoven and Warner (eds.), Laboratory Phonology 7. Berlin: Mouton de Gruyter.
contrasts: seven vowels under stress /i e ɛ a ɔ o u/ against three in unstressed syllables [i ə u]
close-mid versus open-mid vowels: déu [dew] 'god' versus deu [dɛw] 'ten', dóna [ˈdonə] 'gives' versus dona [ˈdɔnə] 'woman', ós [os] versus os [ɔs]
tap /ɾ/ versus trill /r/ between vowels (cera versus serra)
/s/ versus /z/ and /ʃ/ versus /ʒ/ between vowels; affricates /tʃ dʒ/ and marginal /ts dz/
/l/ versus /ʎ/ and /n/ versus /ɲ/, also word-finally (any, ull)
no /v/: written v and b are one phoneme /b/
obstruent voicing is neutralised at the end of a word
geminates in a few words and clusters (il·lusió [ll], setmana [mm], espatlla [ʎʎ], poble [bbl])
allophony: vowel reduction: unstressed /a ɛ e/ are [ə] and unstressed /ɔ o/ are [u]; /i u/ keep their quality; [e] and [o] survive unstressed in a few learned words, compounds and next to /a/ or [ə] in hiatus (teatre [teˈatɾə])
/b d ɡ/ are approximants [β ð ɣ] after vowels and continuants; they stay stops after a pause or a nasal, /d/ also after a lateral

word-final obstruents are voiceless before pause (fred [fɾɛt]); they take the voicing of a following consonant, and word-final sibilants and affricates are voiced before a vowel (els amics [əlz əˈmiks])
/b/ and /ɡ/ are geminated before /l/ after a stressed vowel: poble [ˈpɔbblə], regla [ˈreɡɡlə]
/l/ is velarised [ɫ], most in the coda
word-final r is silent in most words (infinitives, nouns and adjectives in -er, -or: cantar [kənˈta], primer [pɾiˈme]) but kept in some (mar, cor, pur)
the stop of final clusters nt, lt, mp, mb, nd is silent: pont [pɔn], alt [al], camp [kam]
nasals take the place of articulation of the following consonant ([ɱ] before f, [ŋ] before velars, [ɲ] before palatals)
the rhotic contrast is neutralised outside the position between vowels: trill word-initially and after n, l, s; tap or weak trill in the coda and after a consonant in the onset
unstressed /i u/ next to a vowel become glides [j w]
/s z/ are apico-alveolar; /ʃ ʒ/ are alveolo-palatal
phonotactics: word-final consonant clusters are common, up to three consonants with the plural -s (texts, boscs)
/ɾ/ does not begin a word; /ʎ/ and /ɲ/ occur in all positions including word-finally
across words: voicing assimilation, place assimilation of nasals and stops, and elision or gliding of unstressed vowels in contact

stress.type: lexical, on one of the last three syllables
stress.rule: Words ending in a vowel, a vowel plus s, or -en, -in are stressed on the penultimate syllable, other words on the last; all exceptions carry a written accent.
stress.cues: vowel quality (the full seven-vowel set only under stress), duration and pitch; intensity is secondary

rhythm.vowel_reduction: strong in quality, weak in duration: a, e become [ə] and o becomes [u], but reduced vowels are not deleted
rhythm.notes: Catalan has the vowel reduction of stress-timed languages but groups with syllable-timed languages on interval measures: Ramus, Nespor and Mehler (1999) report %V 45.6 and a consonantal interval deviation of 0.045 s, next to Spanish, Italian and French.

length.notes: Consonant length is marginal: geminates arise in clusters (tl, tll, tm, tn, bl, gl) and in learned words (l·l), and are often simplified in casual speech. No figure for their duration is given here.

intonation.declarative: rising accents with a delayed peak on content words before the nucleus (L+<H*), low nuclear accent on the last stressed syllable (L*) and low boundary
intonation.yes_no_question: two patterns: a rising one without particle, low on the last stressed syllable followed by a high rise (L* HH%), and a falling one introduced by unstressed 'que', with a high stretch and a fall on the last stressed syllable (¡H+L* L%)
intonation.wh_question: high on the question word, fall to a low nuclear accent and low boundary; a rising ending is a polite variant
intonation.continuation: rising accent with high boundary (L+H* H%) at the end of non-final phrases
intonation.accent_shape: prenuclear L+<H*: low in the stressed syllable, rise with the peak in the following syllable; nuclear L* in statements
intonation.notes: Labels follow Cat_ToBI (Prieto 2014). Narrow focus uses L+H* on the focused word followed by a low stretch.

problems: no tune set is selected in the voice file, so the generic default tunes are used; the low nuclear accent of statements and the two yes-no question patterns (rising, and falling after 'que') are not modelled
/l/ imports the English phoneme: clear before a vowel, dark only in the coda; Central Catalan /l/ is velarised in all positions
isolated rule errors in common words: rei is [rˈei] with two vowels and reina is [ɾəˈinə] with an initial tap and stress on the i, against [rej] and [ˈrejnə]
a full trill is used in every coda (porta [pˈɔrtə], parlar [pərlˈa]) where the usual realisation is a tap or a short trill
good: vowel reduction is implemented in the phoneme table: unstressed a, e, ɛ become [ə] and o, ɔ become [u], with non-reducing variants for the exceptions (teatre [teˈatɾə])
open and close mid vowels are distinguished by a large exception list (ca_list), since the spelling marks them only under a written accent
approximant [β ð ɣ], final devoicing, voicing assimilation across words and nasal place assimilation are rule-governed in the phoneme table
silent final r, simplified final clusters (pont [pˈɔn], camp [kˈam]), gemination in poble, regla, setmana, and the merger of v with b follow the Central norm

notes: The four Catalan voices share one rule file (ca_rules) and exception list; the dialect voices differ by phoneme table and conditional rules. The Central voice is the base and the most complete.
